claims.claim_summary: An abort policy saves ~18% compute with 83% precision on failing runs.
claims.claim_text_verbatim: Additionally, by deploying an abort policy on top of it, we save ∼18% of the compute that would have been burned on agents heading to failure, and 83% of runs that were interrupted were actually heading to failure (5 out of every 6 aborts were correct).

evidence_spans.source_text: At threshold 0.60 (Table 6), 23.3% of unresolved traces are stopped early at a 20.7% false-stop rate, yielding 17.9% cost savings on the unresolved population.

Because the corpus base rate is heavily skewed toward failure (81% unresolved), the balanced-sample false-stop rates translate to ≈83% precision in deployment: five of six aborted runs would indeed have failed.

One protocol disclosure: the full threshold sweep is reported, and 0.60 is an illustrative threshold selected for exposition after the sweep — not a recommended deployment setting, since it was not chosen on held-out data.

claims.claim_summary: Randomized testing shows high fault recall with zero false interventions on benign runs.
